title: Kyle Schoenfelder reflects on his career and experiences at the University of South Dakota
text:
Kyle Schoenfelder reflects on his career and experiences at the University of South Dakota
Kyle Schoenfelder described on July 8 how his experiences at the University of South Dakota, both as a student and staff member, have shaped his professional journey. Schoenfelder said that studying abroad in the Netherlands and participating in business courses at USD prepared him for future opportunities.
“The Beacom School of Business challenged me in ways I didn’t always expect,” Schoenfelder said. “It was rigorous, and the coursework demanded discipline, critical thinking and a strong work ethic. I appreciate how intentional the school was about developing practical, real-world skills.”
After graduating from USD, Schoenfelder began working full-time at the university while also earning a Master of Arts in educational administration. He currently serves as an academic advisor for over 300 undergraduate business students in the Beacom School of Business. In addition to advising, he teaches a First Year Experience course, supervises peer advising programs, organizes events, and manages global immersion programs that have taken students to several countries including Denmark, Sweden, Estonia, Finland, Spain, Portugal, South Korea and Japan.
Schoenfelder said that although his job has provided international experiences through faculty-led travel programs with students abroad, some of his most meaningful moments occur locally: “There’s a lot to like about advising at USD, but the most rewarding parts occur on an everyday basis. One of the biggest is seeing growth over time,” he said. “You meet students when they’re unsure... Then a semester or two later... They’re making decisions with purpose... Being even a small part of that shift is pretty meaningful.”
He credits USD with shaping not only his career but also personal relationships: “USD has opened doors I didn’t know existed and pushed me to grow in ways I wouldn’t have on my own... Most importantly... USD has surrounded me with the most amazing people,” said Schoenfelder. He noted meeting his wife Ashlin at USD as well as forming lasting friendships and mentorships.
Schoenfelder shared that attending Dakota Days remains one of his favorite traditions: “My friends and I had so much fun attending events during our collegiate career. Now my wife Ashlin and kids Leo and Ruthie join me every year for parade festivities—it's a highlight every single year!”
The University of South Dakota also houses departments such as Sustainability and Environment within its College of Arts & Sciences; this department promotes cultural well-being by enabling students to address environmental challenges through campus action or along local rivers using facilities like Akeley-Lawrence Science Center, according to the official website.
